| | Dear Reader,How about a newspaper that actually loves America?

I'm not just talking about good, old-fashioned flag-waving love of country. I'm talking about much more than that.

It's no secret that most of our national press is ideologically corrupt. It's steeped in agenda-driven coverage and champions grand schemes designed to weaken American ideals and influence on the world stage.

The New York Sun is cut from different cloth. It's a paper that lives and breathes American values. It has done since 1833.

We understand well what makes our country unique and why we must fight for it.

We're sworn to defend and uphold our national parchment, the Constitution of the United States.

We know that equality before the law must be applied in practice and not just in principle.

The Sun's famed 19th century editor, Charles A. Dana, put it this way: "An American who thinks another country is better than this should not go into journalism."

125 years later, we couldn't agree more.

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upliftcoribush?refcode=X_070324_mayorjones [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upliftcoribush?refcode=X_070324_mayorjones] Hi there,
I’m St. Louis Mayor Tishaura Jones, and I am proudly endorsing Cori Bush for Congress.
Can I count on you to join me in supporting her re-election campaign by rushing a donation today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upliftcoribush?refcode=X_070324_mayorjones]
In 2020, Cori Bush defeated a 52-year political dynasty, paving the way for the future of St. Louis and making history as the first Black Congresswoman from Missouri. Months later, in 2021, I was elected the first Black woman mayor of the City of St. Louis. Since then, we have been working together to secure the resources our city needs and be a strong voice of change for St. Louis residents.
When I first took office, I vowed to bring “fresh air” to our beloved city, refusing to stay silent on the racial injustices that have harmed our communities for far too long. I am proud to have had a partner and ally in Cori, who shares the same mission. Together, we’re empowering the city we love and making sure everyone who lives here feels safe, valued, and supported
During her time in office, Cori has delivered over $22 million in direct funding for community projects in St. Louis, supporting critical initiatives such as St. Louis Public Schools, upgrades to our 911 Dispatch System, the St. Louis Housing Authority, and numerous partner organizations dedicated to making our city safer, stronger, and healthier.
Together, we have also distributed nearly half a billion dollars in investments through the American Rescue Plan.
These investments are paving the way for a more just and equitable St. Louis, supporting violence prevention programs, traffic calming measures, and right-to-counsel programs for those at risk of eviction. Cori and I share a vision for St. Louis, where everyone has the opportunity to thrive, and we are unafraid to lead and deliver for our communities.
But we cannot do it alone. We need to show the young women and girls in St. Louis they can have a Mayor and Congresswoman who look like them, and that they can be anything they want to be — and we need your support to continue this vital work and to show the next generation of St. Louisans what it means to be unbought , unbossed , and unafraid .
Will you join us in this fight for a brighter future? Your contribution, no matter the size, will help us build a St. Louis that is safer, more equitable, and filled with hope. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upliftcoribush?refcode=X_070324_mayorjones]

name: Supervisor David Canepa
subject: 2024 July e-newsletter
body:
| | | |
---
| | |
# 2024 July e-newsletter
---
|
---
|
---
| **Let’s celebrate responsibly this Fourth of July!**
---
| Dear friends, From my family to yours, have a wonderful and safe Fourth of July as you celebrate with your friends and families this week. Independence Day reminds us of the long road Americans have traveled to reach the freedoms we have today. But we must all keep in mind that a heat wave and fireworks are a dangerous mix as the National Weather Service has indicated this will a very hot week in the Bay Area with temperatures climbing as high as 100 degrees in Redwood City. With only a handful of cities in the Bay Area selling safe and sane fireworks, including San Bruno and Pacifica in San Mateo County, we must all do our part to have a safe and sane holiday as historically fires related to fireworks peak around the Fourth of July.
---
Mixed with 100-degree temperatures, this could be a very dangerous week for the public, pets, firefighters and first responders as the risk of grass and property fires rise dramatically. As thousands of Bay Area residents flock to the San Mateo County coast this week to escape the heat, I want to warn any residents tempted to purchase safe and sane fireworks in Pacifica, they are strictly illegal to set off in most every corner of the Bay Area and that stiff fines can be imposed. Please be cautious and celebrate responsibly. There are also some great events and fireworks shows planned for July 4 throughout San Mateo County, including in Foster City (pictured above) and the Port of Redwood City. Happy Independence Day.
---
| **Port of Redwood City gets $48 million boost**

The San Mateo County Transportation Authority and Redwood City will receive up to $48 million in Regional Measure 3 toll funds for the $300 million “101/84 Interchange Reimagined” project. This initiative will enhance the Port of Redwood City and ease traffic at the Highway 101/Woodside Road interchange.

As Metropolitan Transportation Commission Legislation Chair, I and fellow Commissioner Gina Papan prioritized these improvements to the full MTC Board of Commissioners June 26, which unanimously approved the request. Kudos to the port’s Executive Director Kristine Zortman and SAMCEDA CEO Rosanne Foust for helping to spearhead this project.

The 1970s era interchange marks the gateway to the Port of Redwood City. But it can no longer accommodate current traffic volumes, presenting challenges to roadway safety, freight mobility and rail movement.

The port is also a certified Federal Staging Area and this investment will help the port be better prepared to save lives and assist in critical recovery efforts when the Bay Area faces the next big quake, which is predicted to be in the next 20 years.

Redwood City and the San Mateo County Transportation Authority plan to start construction in 2027 on a series of safety improvements that will include more than four miles of new bicycle/pedestrian infrastructure as well as improved access for transit shuttles linking the Redwood City Caltrain station and the new San Francisco Bay Ferry terminal planned for the Port of Redwood City.
---
---
|
**Medical Center project hits major milestone** The San Mateo Medical Center campus is undergoing a massive transformation! We’re demolishing outdated buildings, constructing an 87,000 sq. ft. facility, renovating hospital spaces and refreshing the landscaping. This is a big step forward for health care access in San Mateo County.

I was thrilled to join Supervisor Noelia Corzo, Coroner Robert Foucrault, Deputy County Executive Adam Ely, and San Mateo County Health CEO Louise Rogers at a topping off ceremony last week, when the last beam of steel was raised on the project. A big thank you to the union workers on site, Truebeck Construction and Taylor Design.

The event marks a major milestone in this complex multi-phase renovation project that when completed will strive to provide equitable health care access.

PDU provides construction services for all new ground-up capital construction projects for the County of San Mateo properties, including County Office Building 3, the greenest civic center in the United States and now officially open for business.

---
|
**State partners with San Mateo County on loneliness initiative** In January 2024, San Mateo County was the first county in the nation to declare loneliness a public health crisis reporting 45% of San Mateo residents experience loneliness. Half of the U.S. population reports feeling lonely, per the U.S. Surgeon General’s Advisory on the Epidemic of Loneliness, with severe health risks comparable to smoking 15 cigarettes a day. More than half of Americans are disconnected from their communities and say they don’t know their neighbors.

The resolution I sponsored caught the attention of Dr. Elissa Lee, senior adviser with California Volunteers in the Governor’s Office, to reach out my office to promote the Meet 6 Neighbors Pledge, with San Mateo County being the first in the state to pilot the initiative in June.

When neighbors know each other, communities thrive. Knowing six neighbors maximizes your physical and mental health and well-being, and helps us to be better prepared for disasters, makes our streets safer, and overall, a better place to live!

Take this summer pledge to meet 6 neighbors! Ways to do this can range from simply starting a conversation, volunteering to help, or joining/hosting gatherings. To take the pledge, go to [www.Meet6Neighbors.com](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=b6db306c96&e=c0babbc643).
---
| **[](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=2c08264230&e=c0babbc643)
Join us to learn how pets play a role in improving physical and mental well-being** Please join us to learn how pets play a role in improving physical and mental well-being for kids, families and older adults at a special event my office is holding in partnership with the Peninsula Humane Society 4 p.m. to 6 p.m., Tuesday, July 23, 12 Airport Blvd., San Mateo. According to famed UK veterinarian _Dr. Marc Abraham OBE: “The_ _ _ inability to leave the house is a common symptom of loneliness, so having to walk a dog once or twice daily encourages outside physical fitness, lowers rates of obesity and increases the frequency and likelihood of real life human-human interactions.” At our PHS event, you will learn how you can adopt your forever furry friend including dogs, cats, small animals and even exotic animals such as lizards, snakes and turtles [https://phs-spca.org/adopt/exotic-animals/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=aa5548dbec&e=c0babbc643). This event launches the first of many in my office’s “Loneliness t o Light Series.” Abraham continues on the Campaign to End Loneliness blog: “Indeed, having a dog by your side is often the ultimate conversation starter, igniting connections, thus reducing feelings of social isolation. Staying home with a cat, rabbit, or any other furry or feathered friend also offers a degree of companionship and interaction, including fulfilling daily routines, which can all help support and manage long-term mental health issues such as depression, anxiety and loneliness.” [https://www.campaigntoendloneliness.org/the-importance-of-animals-tackling-loneliness-one-pet-at-a-time/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=a6f8f133ca&e=c0babbc643)
---
| **Interns wanted to join our team ** We are looking to add to our great group of interns we are currently working with. If you or someone you know may be interested in applying to my Internship Program, submitting this form is the first step: [https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=dd376aa571&e=c0babbc643). You can also reach out to Mike Richardson on my staff directly with any questions at [tbayudan@smcgov.org](mailto:tbayudan@smcgov.org) .
---
| **Battling food insecurity **
Food insecurity is a problem some residents may still face as we continue to emerge from the pandemic. Here are some resources residents can access: **CalFresh:**
Is a program for people with low-income who meet federal income eligibility rules and want to add to their budget to put healthy and nutritious food on the table. Website: [https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-nutrition/calfresh](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=85980d6fec&e=c0babbc643) Contact: (650) 802-6576, [antorres@smcgov.org](mailto:antorres@smcgov.org) **Daly City Partnership:**
DC Partnership is a local partnership that was formed to guide collaborative efforts and connect our community to services that promote well-being. Check out their website for times and locations. Website: [https://www.dcpartnership.org/covid19/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=9df32ef30a&e=c0babbc643) **Second Harvest Food Bank:**
Second Harvest offers food at various locations throughout San Mateo County listed on its webpage. Website: [https://www.shfb.org/get-food/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=693b94f5c4&e=c0babbc643) Contacts: Call (800) 984-3663 or text GETFOOD to (408) 455-5181 In friendship,
David J. Canepa
---
|
---
|
---
|
---

---

**Our mailing address is:**
Supervisor David Canepa1618 Sullivan497Daly City, CA 94015
[Add us to your address book](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/vcard?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=ea541c4b96)

Want to change how you receive these emails?
You can [update your preferences](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/profile?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=ea541c4b96&e=c0babbc643&c=91ca8a046d) or [unsubscribe from this list](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/unsubscribe?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=ea541c4b96&t=b&e=c0babbc643&c=91ca8a046d).

Hello,
When my husband Adam Frisch ran against Lauren Boebert in 2022, we were the underdogs until the very end.
Adam did not receive any national support. We were heavily out-raised and out-spent by Boebert and her Washington allies.
Ultimately, though, Adam lost in a recount by just 546 votes – the closest race in the entire country.
The worst part is that it wasn’t because we didn’t work hard. Our family, our team, and our volunteers gave it everything we had. We just ran out of money.
In the final weeks of the race, we had to cut back. Right as Boebert was increasing her advertising – right as we _knew_ we were on her heels – we had to pull TV ads, cancel digital buys, and make a lot of hard budget decisions.
Adam might not say it, but I will: If we had had additional resources and been able to fully fund his campaign until the end, Adam would probably be in Congress right now – and Lauren Boebert would be a footnote in a history book.

clean_body: Adam might not say it, but I will. Hello, When my husband Adam Frisch ran against Lauren Boebert in 2022, we were the underdogs until the very end. Adam did not receive any national support. We were heavily out-raised and out-spent by Boebert and her Washington allies. Ultimately, though, Adam lost in a recount by just 546 votes – the closest race in the entire country. The worst part is that it wasn’t because we didn’t work hard. Our family, our team, and our volunteers gave it everything we had. We just ran out of money. In the final weeks of the race, we had to cut back. Right as Boebert was increasing her advertising – right as we knew we were on her heels – we had to pull TV ads, cancel digital buys, and make a lot of hard budget decisions. Adam might not say it, but I will: If we had had additional resources and been able to fully fund his campaign until the end, Adam would probably be in Congress right now – and Lauren Boebert would be a footnote in a history book. It’s part of why Adam announced so early that he was running again. We need to make sure that we have the money to build a campaign that can sustain all the way through to November 5, 2024. But with Lauren Boebert having run off scared, this race is a lot harder. The Super PACs are already attacking Adam, and he’s not taking any money from corporate PACs. **[Packing for Paris: These Coloradans are headed to the 2024 Olympics, Paralympics](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER7 NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Athletes all over Colorado have qualified for the 2024 Paris Olympics and Paralympics and will compete on that world stage this summer.
The Olympics begin July 26 with an opening ceremony and will continue through Aug. 11. The Paralympics will start Aug. 28 and run through Sept. 8.
The Colorado athletes' specialties include volleyball, track and field, climbing, rowing, swimming and more.
Team USA has a map of the United States on its website showing the hometowns of athletes who have currently qualified for the Games. Our list in this story contains those athletes, plus the ones who train here long-term, went to school here, or have Colorado listed as their hometown.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado now has the worst outbreak of bird flu among dairy cattle in the country](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Colorado is experiencing the worst outbreak of bird flu among dairy cattle in the U.S., with nearly one-quarter of its herds affected, most identified in the last month.
* The outbreak began after spillover infections from wild birds, with subsequent spread possibly facilitated through fomite transmission via workers moving between farms.
* Health officials are monitoring dairy workers for flu symptoms, with few tested and no positive cases of bird flu in humans reported from this outbreak.
* The risk to the general public is considered low, but public health officials are prepared to escalate monitoring and testing should the virus mutate to become more dangerous to humans.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[A UFO at Red Rocks? Employees say disc-shaped object appeared in sky, then vanished](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [FOX NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Employees at Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Colorado reported witnessing a large, disc-shaped UFO that hovered and then vanished.
* The craft, described as three stories tall with multiple levels of windows and lights, moved eastward and slowly faded until it became invisible. Observers noted that the UFO disappeared as soon as they began paying close attention to it, suggesting it was aware of being watched.
* The incident has sparked discussions and comparisons to other UFO sightings, including a recent event in Las Vegas analyzed by a crime scene recreation expert using AI, suggesting the presence of "beings" using a cloaking device.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[56 Colorado counties with tax-exempt federal lands getting $48M, that's $2 per acre](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE CENTER SQUARE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Fifty-six Colorado counties will receive a total of $47.8 million through the Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILT) program for about 24 million acres of tax-exempt federal lands, which breaks down to roughly $2 per acre.
* The PILT program was established in 1976 to compensate local governments for losses in property taxes due to the presence of nontaxable federal lands within their jurisdictions.
* The payments are calculated based on a formula considering the county's population, revenue-sharing payments, and the amount of federal land. The funds are intended to help counties finance essential services such as law enforcement, education, and infrastructure, especially given the extensive use of these lands by residents and tourists.
* Mesa County will receive the largest payout of approximately $4.4 million for 1.6 million acres, while Moffat County, with the most federal land at 1.67 million acres, will receive $825,195.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Study: Fentanyl-related deaths cost Colorado estimated $16 billion last year](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* In 2023, Colorado recorded approximately 1,200 fentanyl overdose deaths, costing the state an estimated $16 billion.
* A record 425.6 kilograms of fentanyl was seized in Colorado by the DEA, enough to potentially kill the state's population multiple times, depending on purity.
* Fentanyl-related deaths since 2017 have cost Colorado $56.8 billion, with deaths rising sharply from 130 in 2018 to 1,213 in 2023. Drug overdose deaths now exceed homicide rates in the state, with a significant impact on Denver's homeless population.

Looking for something fun to do tomorrow to celebrate our great country? of Colorado events happening on the 4th and into the weekend! 🇺🇸 This is the Mountain Minute for Wednesday, July 3, 2024. - Heidi Ganahl | | | TODAY'S TOP STORIES Athletes all over Colorado have qualified for the 2024 Paris Olympics and Paralympics and will compete on that world stage this summer. The Olympics begin July 26 with an opening ceremony and will continue through Aug. 11. The Paralympics will start Aug. 28 and run through Sept. 8. The Colorado athletes' specialties include volleyball, track and field, climbing, rowing, swimming and more. Team USA has a map of the United States on its website showing the hometowns of athletes who have currently qualified for the Games. Our list in this story contains those athletes, plus the ones who train here long-term, went to school here, or have Colorado listed as their hometown. | Colorado is experiencing the worst outbreak of bird flu among dairy cattle in the U.S., with nearly one-quarter of its herds affected, most identified in the last month. The outbreak began after spillover infections from wild birds, with subsequent spread possibly facilitated through fomite transmission via workers moving between farms. Health officials are monitoring dairy workers for flu symptoms, with few tested and no positive cases of bird flu in humans reported from this outbreak. The risk to the general public is considered low, but public health officials are prepared to escalate monitoring and testing should the virus mutate to become more dangerous to humans. | Employees at Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Colorado reported witnessing a large, disc-shaped UFO that hovered and then vanished. The craft, described as three stories tall with multiple levels of windows and lights, moved eastward and slowly faded until it became invisible. Observers noted that the UFO disappeared as soon as they began paying close attention to it, suggesting it was aware of being watched. The incident has sparked discussions and comparisons to other UFO sightings, including a recent event in Las Vegas analyzed by a crime scene recreation expert using AI, suggesting the presence of "beings" using a cloaking device. | Fifty-six Colorado counties will receive a total of $47.8 million through the Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILT) program for about 24 million acres of tax-exempt federal lands, which breaks down to roughly $2 per acre. The PILT program was established in 1976 to compensate local governments for losses in property taxes due to the presence of nontaxable federal lands within their jurisdictions. The payments are calculated based on a formula considering the county's population, revenue-sharing payments, and the amount of federal land. The funds are intended to help counties finance essential services such as law enforcement, education, and infrastructure, especially given the extensive use of these lands by residents and tourists. Mesa County will receive the largest payout of approximately $4.4 million for 1.6 million acres, while Moffat County, with the most federal land at 1.67 million acres, will receive $825,195. | In 2023, Colorado recorded approximately 1,200 fentanyl overdose deaths, costing the state an estimated $16 billion. A record 425.6 kilograms of fentanyl was seized in Colorado by the DEA, enough to potentially kill the state's population multiple times, depending on purity. Fentanyl-related deaths since 2017 have cost Colorado $56.8 billion, with deaths rising sharply from 130 in 2018 to 1,213 in 2023. Drug overdose deaths now exceed homicide rates in the state, with a significant impact on Denver's homeless population. | ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ BY KELLY SLOAN | COMMENTARY | JUNE 29 The progressive 's unquenchable appetite for exacting every last ounce of flesh from those who have accumulated more wealth than Bernie Sanders thinks appropriate may have gotten a bit of unsolicited help from the Supreme Court last week. | | I want to personally thank you for being a part of this grassroots team. Without you, our work wouldn't be as strong. Your support is what allows us to move the needle for voting rights across the country. Last week marked the somber anniversary of _Shelby County v. Holder_. Eleven years ago, the Supreme Court found important parts of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 unconstitutional — which ushered in a flood of voter suppression laws and practices targeting Black and brown voters. **This is why our work is so important — especially in an election year.** We sound the alarm wherever and whenever voter suppression is taking place, in Georgia and beyond. If anti-voter politicians gain power this year, they’ll double down on their voter suppression tactics for future elections and launch challenges against the laws that protect our right to vote. That’s why I’m grateful to have activists like you on Team Fair Fight at this critical juncture for the future of our country. We’re committed to working towards a democracy where every voter has the opportunity to make their voice heard. Thank you for doing your part. Lauren Groh-Wargo

Hi friends – thank you SO much for your generous support during my end-of-quarter fundraising push before the FEC deadline.
I know you’re getting a lot of requests for help, especially as November draws nearer and focus on the election increases. I want you to know that what you’re doing really matters.
Not just donating (THANK YOU for doing that, because it truly helps!), but also reading these emails, sharing your thoughts, and staying involved.
Sometimes staying tuned in is a challenge in itself, but it’s one of the most critical things we can do right now. The extreme Republicans who want to expand their power are relying on us to get tired, get complacent, and let them get ahead – but if we stay engaged and refuse to stop fighting for our shared values, we can win .
So thank you, from the bottom of my heart, for everything you’re doing.
Talk soon,
Sara

clean_body: Every contribution counts, Peter. | = Hi Peter, You probably know by now that we just submitted our quarterly fundraising totals to the FEC — a requirement for all organizations contributing to campaigns to promote transparency in the electoral process. What you might not know is that this year, our monthly numbers are getting reported too. That matters, and it's part of why every contribution to EMILYs List counts so much. = | = First, a peek behind the curtain: This cycle, we've switched to ActBlue, the online contribution platform used by most Democratic campaigns and organizations. ActBlue is a hybrid PAC that, similar to all PACs, can opt to submit monthly fundraising totals instead of quarterly totals in electoral on-years. But guess what? Republicans' primary fundraising platform has opted to avoid publishing these monthly totals — which means we'll only find out how much they've brought in once every three months. So, what does this mean for us, Peter? It means the GOP knows exactly how much we're raising every month, so they can plan their targeted attack spending against our candidates accordingly. Team, I don’t know about you, but I’m tired of how often the Supreme Court is in the news these days. There’s a new story every other day about Justices Alito and Thomas and their ties to the radical right, and far too many decisions in the past few years demonstrate the partisan activism of the court. **That’s why I believe it’s time we expand the Supreme Court.** In our democracy, the Court is not supposed to be a bastion of partisan interests and biased Justices. But Donald Trump abused his presidential powers to appoint three right-wing justices to the Court. **[The number of seats on the Supreme Court has changed several times before, and it needs to change again. If you agree, add your name in support of the _Judiciary Act_ , legislation that would help right Donald Trump’s wrongs and restore the balance of the Supreme Court.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/88177504/483366660/777135479?refcode=AU_TSM_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20240703_AM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTU1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2OTdhNDM4My01NjM5LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=A6ce0k8Wpfe4rwjFbkMBH2rplkpWw92lxCwMO3kgQRo=&emci=e4d1c561-9d38-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=697a4383-5639-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=6227932)** | [EXPAND THE SUPREME COURT](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/88177505/483366661/777135479?refcode=AU_TSM_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20240703_AM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTU1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2OTdhNDM4My01NjM5LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=A6ce0k8Wpfe4rwjFbkMBH2rplkpWw92lxCwMO3kgQRo=&emci=e4d1c561-9d38-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=697a4383-5639-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=6227932)

## **On Second Amendment issues, Nick gets an "A"**
##
### Mary Peltola gets an "F" — (almost) the worst possible.

Dear Friends,

I am thrilled to announce that I have been awarded an "A" rating from Gun Owners of America (GOA), a testament to my unwavering commitment to defending our Second Amendment rights. In contrast, incumbent Democrat Mary Peltola has received an "F" rating from GOA, highlighting her abysmal record on gun rights. According to GOA, an "F" rating signifies a "philosophically committed anti-gunner" who consistently votes against the interests of gun owners.

As it turns out, **only one person in Congress has scored lower than Mary Peltola on gun rights — her ally Nancy Pelosi **(who scored an "F-").

The Constitution is unequivocal: the right of the people to keep and bear arms SHALL NOT be infringed. I stand 100% supportive of this fundamental right. Don't let Mary Peltola's glitzy ads fool you; her record for gun owners is exceptionally poor.

In Congress, I will continue to work tirelessly to protect your Second Amendment rights and address the real issues behind violence. Together, we can build a safer and freer America.

Thank you for your support.

Best regards,

Nick Begich

| | Dear Fellow Patriot, If you opened this letter because you remember my playing days with the Dodgers and the Padres, thank you. Having you and all of America's baseball fans cheering for me and Davey Lopes, Bill Russell, Ron Cey and the rest of the guys as we battled Reggie Jackson, Thurman Munson and the Yankees... ...well, as they say, "Those were the days." But this email - isn't about baseball in fact, it's an email I never thought I'd be writing to you. **[Today, I'm asking you to help me defeat the radical Adam Schiff for a seat in the United States Senate.](http://links.myfreedomnews.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=d7fbbda27b0a446fa5ea779324443a0f&_e=ozUd_FV2AWDIRQkjNgTZ3sNlE1SFBA4lXu8IJMZjSFPIYEjxc6MzL19YCZ4amwtyzuUjB0BZ0PhEjRNUCkY-NJbhkMCs4boRxfbzr8zL0Xm2aYRI5IKCXvgSApFntVmDA5Rx0H-gkJZExKiEMpNvp8-lZJM4JnIu_V_zSn4ldqU7i8_6TBJ11Ufl9T717qkSaCNRTDcM5kD4OzacM4N1N8In6g-_GxSHQE5rjuRrGKSzG6mGO14C_5z6YnaStBdZXos_iGgCZle2YYVs9JzAHaEP7aoBqPfhdOkFDVGgpWGK21Qj2sz2SODdkLcGSAbWRO68I2YkbmmHMmYSNliolS3rJeIbLlYY1FyQEmfKmE9d1E5w3Yb6SY3bpGSlU1_RCwx6x0LohxtxFvK7hEm6dg%3D%3D)** Today, I'm asking you to help me start a Republican Comeback Rally that folks will be talking about for generations to come. Because when you think about it, those 'good-ol' days of the 1970s weren't as good as we tend to first remember. Baseball was just a welcome distraction from the gloom and malaise that had settled on our country thanks to one failed Democrat policy after another. I'm running for the United States Senate because 2024 America is starting to look a lot like 1970s America. You remember what it was like: ► Not only were gas prices sky high, Carter's rationing meant we could only buy gas on even or odd days depending on our license plate numbers. **_Remember?_** ► Eleven Israeli athletes were slaughtered at the Olympic Village in Munich by terrorists. _**Remember?**_ ► Fifty-two Americans were held hostage for 444 days by terrorists in Iran. _**Remember?**_ Democrat policies had brought America to its knees. And now, as Yogi Berra used to say, "It's deja vu all over again." There's fear of walking down the street because of rampant crime, homelessness, and drug addiction. The cost of living is exploding and for the first time causing more people to leave California. Joe Biden, Adam Schiff and the rest of the Democrats don't care one bit that Americans are having a hard time. I'd go even further to say they welcome the misery so they can keep folks down and dependent. And I wouldn't blame you if you said, "Steve, I'm afraid America's best days are behind us." But listen, here's something I also want you to remember... **_We_ _Republicans_ pulled our country out of that 1970's Democratic malaise by electing Ronald Reagan. ** **We put classic conservative values at the heart of everything we did.** **And America became a shining city upon a hill once more.** **_We_ _can_ _do_ _that_ _again._** **It starts by stunning the Democrats with a Senate win in California.** **But there's no way I can pull it off without you.** [**That's why I'm asking you to rush back your _Garvey for Senate_ contribution of $35 or more right away. **](http://links.myfreedomnews.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=d7fbbda27b0a446fa5ea779324443a0f&_e=ozUd_FV2AWDIRQkjNgTZ3sNlE1SFBA4lXu8IJMZjSFPIYEjxc6MzL19YCZ4amwtyzuUjB0BZ0PhEjRNUCkY-NJbhkMCs4boRxfbzr8zL0Xm2aYRI5IKCXvgSApFntVmDA5Rx0H-gkJZExKiEMpNvp8-lZJM4JnIu_V_zSn4ldqU7i8_6TBJ11Ufl9T717qkSaCNRTDcM5kD4OzacM4N1N8In6g-_GxSHQE5rjuRrGKSzG6mGO14C_5z6YnaStBdZuLOG9GwCUsqmb6XVh0kBV7MQATPhPqlaEq0GVEk5Vo30MmECB5X53k2iKNBxC2GxfP3zqcxEZ-DXaAsZD6VxqzIkgrosLUvPFPmWZ23soMiLiJdriwWsqQj_VgyIqpaRt7Qz6_LmrPedtLh_ao5RJw%3D%3D) I'm sorry for the urgency but Election Day is just six months away... And in that time, we need to build a 58-county, grassroots campaign capable of defeating Adam Schiff who has ActBlue allies and a war chest he's assembled during his two decades in Washington, D.C. That may seem daunting, but I know with your help, I can beat him in November. Why? First... I've lived and worked in California for over 50 years, and I can tell you -- voters here have had it with the Democrats like I've never seen before. They are hungry for change, and if you and I work together to reach voters in every neighborhood, on every beach, in every corner of California... I know we can turn this historic opportunity into a Republican win. Second... you know I'm not a career politician. But I do have the _one_ _thing_ a Republican needs to get elected in California... ...name recognition. I'm no Schwarzenegger and I'd certainly never dare compare myself to President Reagan. But California voters know me. And Adam Schiff and the Democrats are shaking in their boots seeing how quickly I rose in the polls after entering the race. clean_body: (and you played a big part in it!) | Last week marked a pivotal victory for our climate movement: We forced Big Oil to drop its dangerous California referendum from the November ballot! ICYMI: Big Oil poured $61 million into overturning a crucial law (SB 1137) that was meant to protect Californians by prohibiting new oil and gas wells within 3,200 feet of homes, schools, hospitals, and other sensitive areas. That includes a massive disinformation campaign to trick voters into believing these essential protections were government overreach. But thanks to the relentless efforts of Jane Fonda and the Campaign for a Safe and Healthy California, a coalition of frontline community climate activists, we prevailed! SB 1137 is now the law of the land in California. = = Let’s be clear: This win didn’t come easy. Jane never gave up on this fight, and you never gave up on her. YOU played a crucial role in this victory. Your donations, time, and passion fueled our efforts and kept the pressure on Big Oil. This win is proof that when we unite and fight for what’s right, we can triumph over corporate greed to secure lasting progress. But look, the fight isn’t over. Big Oil isn’t backing down — they realized they couldn’t get the voters on their side, so instead, they’re already plotting to sue to overturn this law in the courts. We know they’ll come back with a vengeance, so we need to be ready. That means electing climate champions at the state and local level across the country who are willing to pass bold legislation like SB 1137. | | | **July 3rd, 2024** |
---|---|---|---
| | | **Senate Update: Rebuilding the Bridge, Supporting Communities, and Honoring a Maryland Hero** It's an understatement to say that this has been a challenging time at home and abroad. Overseas we are confronting the continued rise of authoritarianism, the ongoing wars in Ukraine and Gaza, China's aggressive actions, and serious conflicts ranging from Haiti to Sudan. At home, we also face threats to our democracy and freedom. The recent decisions by the Supreme Court have been especially alarming. By striking down the Chevron deference doctrine and conferring unprecedented, king-like immunity on the office of the president, this Court has made dangerous power grabs and endangered democracy itself. These are just a few examples of the many outrageous decisions this far-right Court has delivered, which have ranged from the despicable Dobbs decision two years ago, to their more recent rulings striking down common-sense gun protection measures and stripping away critical environmental protections. Many of these decisions have also shined a light on the troubling influence of outside right-wing donors and groups on our Supreme Court Justices - yet another reason we need to pass legislation I have cosponsored to establish a binding, enforceable code of ethics at the Supreme Court. Simply put, our highest court in the land should not have the lowest ethical standards. I will keep fighting back against these dangerous decisions by the Supreme Court while working to protect our institutions, our democracy, and our rule of law. As we confront these threats to democracy and freedom at home and abroad, we must also press ahead on our domestic agenda. In the last three years, we've made enormous progress in modernizing our infrastructure, deploying more clean energy, caring for our veterans, and much, much more. At the same time, we must continue our work to cut costs for American families, increase affordable housing, and make health care and child care more accessible and affordable. Throughout this politically turbulent period, I have never taken my eye off Maryland - and our critical work to support our local communities. In the past few months alone, we have delivered key investments for important initiatives across the state, stood united to secure critical resources in the wake of the Key Bridge collapse, and announced the awarding of the Distinguished Service Cross to a Maryland and national hero, Waverly Woodson, in honor of his service during World War II. As we prepare to celebrate our independence, I want to share some of these successes with you. They remind us of what we can accomplish when we work together.
## Honoring Waverly Woodson
A few days before the 80th anniversary of the Allied invasion of Normandy on D-Day, [I was proud to announce that World War II veteran Waverly B. Woodson Jr. is posthumously receiving a long-overdue honor.](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-announces-award-of-distinguished-service-cross-to-d-day-veteran-waverly-woodson%23%3a%7e%3atext%3dToday%252C%2520U.S.%2520Senator%2520Chris%2520Van%2cNormandy%2520of%2520World%2520War%2520II.&redir_log=623352908051484) Woodson, a 21-year-old Black medic and a staff sergeant in the 320th Barrage Balloon Battalion, spent over 30 hours on Omaha Beach treating his fellow soldiers amid intense combat and saving an estimated 200 lives. He did this all despite being wounded before he even reached the shore. Mr. Woodson was born and raised in Pennsylvania, but following the war he settled in Clarksburg, Maryland, where his widow, Joann, and members of his family still live today. Even during one of America's finest hours, Waverly Woodson's valor stood out. His contemporaries, including his commander, wanted to recommend him for the Medal of Honor. But the award never came; he was overlooked because of the color of his skin. Not a single Black World War II soldier received a Medal of Honor until 1997. Mr. Woodson's family has spent years working with my office, the First Army, World War II historians, and others to secure the recognition he deserves. I have been proud to work alongside them in this effort. That's why on June 3rd, [I was especially pleased to announce that the Army has posthumously awarded Waverly Woodson the Distinguished Service Cross](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2ftwitter.com%2fhome%3fmx%3d1&redir_log=841186938204199) - the second-highest U.S. military honor and the highest award the Army can bestow on its own authority. This award recognizes Mr. Woodson's bravery and selflessness and marks a major step forward in our efforts to right a historic wrong. While we have more work to do to fully honor Mr. Woodson's service, this is a momentous recognition.
## Rebuilding the Key Bridge
On March 26th, the container ship Dali collided with the Key Bridge outside Baltimore City. The tragic accident killed six construction workers, destroyed a vital piece of regional infrastructure, and shut down Baltimore's port. The impact of the collapse has been felt across the city, our state, and our nation. In response to this terrible tragedy, we came together. Without the spirit of unity that has prevailed since the collapse, it wouldn't have been possible to clear the debris and reopen the Port of Baltimore's deep federal navigation channel in less than three months. I am grateful for law enforcement at the scene who stopped traffic before the bridge collapsed and saved lives, the first responders and emergency crews who rushed to the scene, and our federal, state, and local partners who have stepped up to support the Marylanders affected by this disaster and reopen the Port. Partner agencies swiftly formed a [Unified Command](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.keybridgeresponse2024.com%2f&redir_log=921499681824257) to manage the multi-pronged effort. Thanks to the tireless work of their dive teams, all of the victims' bodies were recovered. On June 12th, 11 weeks after the collision, the federal navigation channel was completely reopened, allowing the Port of Baltimore to resume full operations. As ships resume their calls, more longshoremen and other workers will be back on the job and the entire state and local economy will benefit. While we have taken great strides to recover from this accident, my heart remains with the family and loved ones of those we lost. We are also still at the beginning of a long process to rebuild the bridge itself. The collapse was a national disaster and merits a national response. That's why federal team Maryland immediately worked - and succeeded - to include the bridge replacement project in the Federal Highway Administration's Emergency Relief Program for Disaster-Damaged Highways and Bridges, which guarantees that the federal government will fund 90% of the replacement efforts. Then, I joined with Senator Cardin, Congressman Mfume, and the entire delegation to [introduce the bipartisan Baltimore BRIDGE Relief Act](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fteam-maryland-introduces-legislation-to-ensure-100-percent-federal-support-for-replacing-the-francis-scott-key-bridge&redir_log=968697067241189), which would ensure 100% federal funding. Since the beginning, President Biden has pledged to work with us to deliver those resources. On June 28th, the White House recommitted to this effort by [laying out an emergency funding package](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fChrisVanHollen%2fstatus%2f1806774448164667892&redir_log=952699341622332) that honors our commitment that the federal government will cover the cost of rebuilding the Key Bridge and provides the money Maryland and other states need to address this and other disasters. As we continue these efforts, the National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash in order to collect the facts, prevent future disasters, and hold all responsible parties accountable. The federal government will receive funds that may be recovered from third parties and litigation to help offset the costs of the rebuilding. Just as we came together when the bridge first fell, we will continue working together until it has been rebuilt.
## Supporting Maryland Communities
Earlier this year, Congress finally was able to move forward on a bipartisan basis to pass a [full funding bill for the 2024 fiscal year](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-statement-on-funding-package&redir_log=139045197332649). While not perfect, the legislation put to bed MAGA Republicans' threat of a shameful shutdown - and it includes over $200 million in direct funding we fought to secure for community projects throughout Maryland. Recently, I've had the chance to celebrate some of these wins across our counties, cities, and towns. I visited Prince George's County with Senator Cardin and Congressman Ivey, where we [delivered over $3.4 million for water infrastructure](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-cardin-ivey-celebrate-earth-day-with-34-million-federal-investment-in-prince-georges-county-water-infrastructure&redir_log=616486681741241). These investments, in communities including Bladensburg, Cottage City, Cheverly, and Bowie, will improve the health of the Anacostia River, upgrade stormwater infrastructure, and mitigate flooding. Protecting water quality and shoring up our communities' defenses against flooding are critical to the health and safety of our residents. I also recently spent time in West Baltimore, where we are making transformative investments and reversing decades of disinvestment. Senator Cardin, Congressman Mfume, and I joined community leaders to visit the Y in Druid Hill, a century-old institution that has long anchored neighborhoods like Upton, Sandtown-Winchester, Harlem Park, and Druid Heights. During Jim Crow and segregation, the Y provided a pool to Black Baltimoreans - including a young Thurgood Marshall - who were unjustly barred from other indoor swimming facilities. Today, it provides health and fitness resources, early education and summer programs, and transitional housing for young women with children. So much has changed in Baltimore over the years, but the Druid Hill Y has been a constant. I was proud to help [secure $1.2 million](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-announces-senate-passage-of-appropriations-package-with-over-40-million-for-maryland-infrastructure-rural-development-military-construction-projects&redir_log=895650003661506) to preserve the Y and refurbish it for future generations. In Northwest Baltimore, I visited Park West, a Federally Qualified Health Center that provides care for everyone - regardless of their ability to pay. Over the course of two fiscal years, we have [delivered $2.5 million](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-cardin-celebrate-45-million-in-direct-federal-investments-in-west-baltimore-to-support-small-business-workforce-development-health-care-initiatives&redir_log=938462848131490) to help Park West renovate their facilities, expand their services, and integrate new disciplines like youth mental health. In addition to these visits, I spent a day on the Eastern Shore with local business leaders, farmers, and others in Dorchester, Queen Anne's and Talbot Counties. In Cambridge, I [held a roundtable](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-meets-with-eastern-shore-crab-houses-highlights-efforts-to-support-seafood-industrys-employment-needs&redir_log=10037933671173) with the men and women who power our local seafood industry at the J.M. Clayton Seafood Company. During our discussion, we spoke about the challenges these businesses face due to our broken H-2B visa program. Maryland's seafood businesses, most of which are small and family-owned, have long relied on seasonal workers. If workers are not available to process crabs when harvest occurs, businesses face closure - either for the season or permanently. I have repeatedly worked with the Department of Homeland Security to issue extra visas, but we need a sustainable solution. That's why I introduced the bipartisan Save our Seafood Act to [fix the H-2B program for the seafood industry](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-cardin-announce-availability-of-over-130000-h-2b-visas-for-fiscal-year-2024-and-bipartisan-legislation-to-support-seafood-industrys-long-term-workforce-needs&redir_log=86643253741532). While we push to improve worker protections and strengthen our immigration system across the board, this legislation is a vital piece of the puzzle for our seafood industry. In Queenstown, I hosted local family farmers, members of Maryland agricultural associations, and Maryland Secretary of Agriculture Kevin Atticks to [discuss the upcoming Farm Bill](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.stardem.com%2fnews%2flocal_news%2fvan-hollen-hears-from-eastern-shore-farmers-on-farm-bill%2farticle_026c4d80-e3ae-11ee-963f-6f2d53f858f6.html&redir_log=341561955651955) and how we can include provisions that boost Maryland agriculture. We depend on farmers to put food on our tables, expand our economy, and create jobs. As farmers face supply chain issues, rising costs, and fluctuating prices, progress on the Farm Bill has been delayed for too long. I am committed to working towards its passage and preventing members of Congress from playing politics with critical programs. I am also fighting to strengthen protections like crop insurance, dairy margin coverage, and bird flu compensation for farmers who face unexpected calamities. Finally, the next Farm Bill must continue to provide strong support for the voluntary programs Maryland farmers use to help preserve the Chesapeake Bay. In Talbot County, I visited Tilghman Island Seafood, the only USDA-certified blue catfish processing facility on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Blue catfish are an invasive species that menace the Chesapeake Bay and rivers throughout Maryland, devouring native species like rockfish, shad, and blue crabs. Fortunately, there's always a bigger fish: us. To get blue catfish out of our waters and onto our dinner tables, I worked with Senator Cardin and Congressman Harris to [include $4.5 million](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-cardin-visit-seafood-processing-business-highlight-efforts-to-accelerate-blue-catfish-processing&redir_log=315106319751132) in the Fiscal Year 2024 funding bill to help small food processors like Tilghman Island Seafood. There's more to do to address this challenge, but we're committed to working with our local watermen to tackle it head-on. In late June, Senator Cardin and I visited Frederick and Howard Counties to highlight [$2.8 million of support](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15547.41259774.6663446.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-cardin-visit-frederick-howard-counties-to-mark-over-28-million-in-direct-federal-investments-for-infrastructure-emergency-services-and-small-business-development&redir_log=496932994821589) for three vital community projects. In the Village of Burkittsville, which has repeatedly experienced flooding, we secured $385,000 to upgrade stormwater infrastructure and better protect local homes and businesses. In Frederick, we joined County Executive Fitzwater and other local leaders to highlight a $1.2 million investment in a solar-powered microgrid for the County's emergency response systems. When disaster strikes and Frederick County falls dark, our emergency facilities and personnel - powered by this microgrid - will be able to keep our communities safe. Finally, we and Congressman John Sarbanes visited the Columbia headquarters of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), where we recently secured $1.1 million for their Federal Lab Leveraging Innovation to Projects Pilot Program. In a roundtable with local small business owners, we discussed how this funding will empower entrepreneurs in tech and health to partner with Maryland's 70 federal labs to develop new products and improve the quality of life for everyone. These visits - and the investments they highlight - represent just a sampling of what we're doing in our communities and the funds we've delivered. Within the Fiscal Year 2024 funding bill, I was proud that we secured investments for local projects in all 23 of Maryland's counties and Baltimore City. And don't worry - we're not stopping at just these. Next up, I'll be headed to St. Mary's and Charles Counties.
### Celebrating our Democracy on Independence Day
This Independence Day, as we celebrate the American Revolution and the spirit of 1776, let us rededicate ourselves to building a more perfect union with liberty and justice for all. Our democracy depends on our participation. I am grateful to all Americans who take seriously their duties of citizenship to make our great experiment in self-government a success. James McHenry, Maryland's delegate to the Constitutional Convention, wrote in his diaries about a famous exchange between Elizabeth Willing Powell and Benjamin Franklin. He wrote, "A lady asked Dr. Franklin: 'Well Doctor what have we, what have we got a monarchy or a republic?' 'A republic,' replied the Doctor, 'if you can keep it.'" This was a prescient warning - we must work together to keep it. Many thanks for being a partner in this progress, and Happy Independence Day!
Chris Van Hollen

clean_body: | | | | ---|--- | | | July 3rd, 2024 | ---|---|---|--- | | | Senate Update: Rebuilding the Bridge, Supporting Communities, and Honoring a Maryland Hero It's an understatement to say that this has been a challenging time at home and abroad. Overseas we are confronting the continued rise of authoritarianism, the ongoing wars in Ukraine and Gaza, China's aggressive actions, and serious conflicts ranging from Haiti to Sudan. At home, we also face threats to our democracy and freedom. The recent decisions by the Supreme Court have been especially alarming. By striking down the Chevron deference doctrine and conferring unprecedented, king-like immunity on the office of the president, this Court has made dangerous power grabs and endangered democracy itself. These are just a few examples of the many outrageous decisions this far-right Court has delivered, which have ranged from the despicable Dobbs decision two years ago, to their more recent rulings striking down common-sense gun protection measures and stripping away critical environmental protections. Many of these decisions have also shined a light on the troubling influence of outside right-wing donors and groups on our Supreme Court Justices - yet another reason we need to pass legislation I have cosponsored to establish a binding, enforceable code of ethics at the Supreme Court. Simply put, our highest court in the land should not have the lowest ethical standards. I will keep fighting back against these dangerous decisions by the Supreme Court while working to protect our institutions, our democracy, and our rule of law. As we confront these threats to democracy and freedom at home and abroad, we must also press ahead on our domestic agenda. In the last three years, we've made enormous progress in modernizing our infrastructure, deploying more clean energy, caring for our veterans, and much, much more. At the same time, we must continue our work to cut costs for American families, increase affordable housing, and make health care and child care more accessible and affordable. Throughout this politically turbulent period, I have never taken my eye off Maryland - and our critical work to support our local communities. In the past few months alone, we have delivered key investments for important initiatives across the state, stood united to secure critical resources in the wake of the Key Bridge collapse, and announced the awarding of the Distinguished Service Cross to a Maryland and national hero, Waverly Woodson, in honor of his service during World War II. As we prepare to celebrate our independence, I want to share some of these successes with you. They remind us of what we can accomplish when we work together. Honoring Waverly Woodson A few days before the 80th anniversary of the Allied invasion of Normandy on D-Day, Woodson, a 21-year-old Black medic and a staff sergeant in the 320th Barrage Balloon Battalion, spent over 30 hours on Omaha Beach treating his fellow soldiers amid intense combat and saving an estimated 200 lives. He did this all despite being wounded before he even reached the shore. Mr. Woodson was born and raised in Pennsylvania, but following the war he settled in Clarksburg, Maryland, where his widow, Joann, and members of his family still live today. Even during one of America's finest hours, Waverly Woodson's valor stood out. His contemporaries, including his commander, wanted to recommend him for the Medal of Honor. But the award never came; he was overlooked because of the color of his skin. Not a single Black World War II soldier received a Medal of Honor until 1997. Mr. Woodson's family has spent years working with my office, the First Army, World War II historians, and others to secure the recognition he deserves. I have been proud to work alongside them in this effort. That's why on June 3rd, - the second-highest U.S. military honor and the highest award the Army can bestow on its own authority. This award recognizes Mr. Woodson's bravery and selflessness and marks a major step forward in our efforts to right a historic wrong. While we have more work to do to fully honor Mr. Woodson's service, this is a momentous recognition. Rebuilding the Key Bridge On March 26th, the container ship Dali collided with the Key Bridge outside Baltimore City. The tragic accident killed six construction workers, destroyed a vital piece of regional infrastructure, and shut down Baltimore's port. The impact of the collapse has been felt across the city, our state, and our nation. In response to this terrible tragedy, we came together. Without the spirit of unity that has prevailed since the collapse, it wouldn't have been possible to clear the debris and reopen the Port of Baltimore's deep federal navigation channel in less than three months. I am grateful for law enforcement at the scene who stopped traffic before the bridge collapsed and saved lives, the first responders and emergency crews who rushed to the scene, and our federal, state, and local partners who have stepped up to support the Marylanders affected by this disaster and reopen the Port. Partner agencies swiftly formed a to manage the multi-pronged effort. Thanks to the tireless work of their dive teams, all of the victims' bodies were recovered. On June 12th, 11 weeks after the collision, the federal navigation channel was completely reopened, allowing the Port of Baltimore to resume full operations. As ships resume their calls, more longshoremen and other workers will be back on the job and the entire state and local economy will benefit. While we have taken great strides to recover from this accident, my heart remains with the family and loved ones of those we lost. We are also still at the beginning of a long process to rebuild the bridge itself. The collapse was a national disaster and merits a national response. That's why federal team Maryland immediately worked - and succeeded - to include the bridge replacement project in the Federal Highway Administration's Emergency Relief Program for Disaster-Damaged Highways and Bridges, which guarantees that the federal government will fund 90% of the replacement efforts. Then, I joined with Senator Cardin, Congressman Mfume, and the entire delegation to , which would ensure 100% federal funding. Since the beginning, President Biden has pledged to work with us to deliver those resources. On June 28th, the White House recommitted to this effort by that honors our commitment that the federal government will cover the cost of rebuilding the Key Bridge and provides the money Maryland and other states need to address this and other disasters. As we continue these efforts, the National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash in order to collect the facts, prevent future disasters, and hold all responsible parties accountable. The federal government will receive funds that may be recovered from third parties and litigation to help offset the costs of the rebuilding. Just as we came together when the bridge first fell, we will continue working together until it has been rebuilt. Supporting Maryland Communities Earlier this year, Congress finally was able to move forward on a bipartisan basis to pass a . While not perfect, the legislation put to bed MAGA Republicans' threat of a shameful shutdown - and it includes over $200 million in direct funding we fought to secure for community projects throughout Maryland. Recently, I've had the chance to celebrate some of these wins across our counties, cities, and towns. I visited Prince George's County with Senator Cardin and Congressman Ivey, where we . These investments, in communities including Bladensburg, Cottage City, Cheverly, and Bowie, will improve the health of the Anacostia River, upgrade stormwater infrastructure, and mitigate flooding. Protecting water quality and shoring up our communities' defenses against flooding are critical to the health and safety of our residents. I also recently spent time in West Baltimore, where we are making transformative investments and reversing decades of disinvestment. Today, it provides health and fitness resources, early education and summer programs, and transitional housing for young women with children. So much has changed in Baltimore over the years, but the Druid Hill Y has been a constant. I was proud to help to preserve the Y and refurbish it for future generations. | | Dear Friend,

There's a tough question that I have to ask you on this fine day.

Here it is...What is true about the world?

Tough, right?

It's a question mankind has asked since ancient times--since creation itself. So, if you don't know the answer, that's fine (if you do, email me because I would love to know more!).

This question is especially pressing today because of the growing power modern humans have to change and manipulate the material world.

That's one of the reasons we released our free online course, **" The Great Principles of Chemistry."**

Why chemistry?

For one, this course brings a core subject studied at Hillsdale College to millions of Americans, including you.

More fundamentally, we study chemistry as part of our liberal arts education at Hillsdale because the sciences help us understand important aspects of reality. It helps us think about our role as humans in the world around us and reveals the framework, implications, and potential for human life.

[](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=858e00e68d1d47a6940c29f31a84c6e4&_e=zPLXpoSEnl2IbQasHi7p5clTlC9nNRb_JMwMkedA4E03Kvg41z0F3T8xlFZQbyBxKn_GHac6puavvbCR_SUtNk9uERZDjTTqkNy7Gr0BuE_WYESv-rDiBptCFsDwSEH8PY0D3dRmwOo0FTQ3i7OHXYofcGx3dvfeHJfKTsCROEVexPqsyRpm1lTjwCjWN9Sfu3dvPYln8i_d7iGHpNlszzaUMgCJuzch4Jg9rs_6tRap3XSJ2JJQFT9vVBi8n-lZbOOdgNxQCBbPRsnjykU_TZi33B4pnEsxN3L02227zMA-lVlvB9mRF0XnbeTf6dbY7XQj7qeTK5zigReFA9kgesTymjDLOB3bJuwjsUPhp7rmxjvhucH7xpIwXyjwB_DsZ0fO6VaxdxLcNuhUy4CVAnEhluNkiG15MuUmtlro0GQ%3D) Like all our courses, **" The Great Principles of Chemistry"** contains stunning visuals, study guides, quizzes, and in this case, hands-on experiments. This content is especially well-suited for science teachers, homeschool parents, or lifelong learners.

And our online courses are free. That's why we depend on the generosity of people like you to help us share the course with as many people as possible.

Would you consider making a tax-deductible donation to help promote this course?

**For any donation of $100 or more, you will receive this beautiful DVD box set for "The Great Principles of Chemistry," by clicking the link below:

**[https://secured.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale/principles-of-chemistry](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=858e00e68d1d47a6940c29f31a84c6e4&_e=zPLXpoSEnl2IbQasHi7p5clTlC9nNRb_JMwMkedA4E03Kvg41z0F3T8xlFZQbyBxKn_GHac6puavvbCR_SUtNk9uERZDjTTqkNy7Gr0BuE_WYESv-rDiBptCFsDwSEH8PY0D3dRmwOo0FTQ3i7OHXYofcGx3dvfeHJfKTsCROEVexPqsyRpm1lTjwCjWN9Sfu3dvPYln8i_d7iGHpNlszzaUMgCJuzch4Jg9rs_6tRap3XSJ2JJQFT9vVBi8n-lZgceJehl4-odGy6Gs5BsCL8PYghiVGOSQLmUjYDTqzcmhdqU4SvlBLf9CQjVEFPOy5-4yuIytiF6H_2MKG9TrTAf6fqUnOybcMzFb3iZ9RPSAEJhCRJL68-e8E_8Fr6c8Hc4C6oTJbfBwqqlyPqU712Yf2xkUSPyqVdK6WOovr-0%3D)

The proper study of chemistry helps us understand the world and inspires wonder and awe at the beauty of creation and its Creator.

For these reasons, please join us in helping others gain a greater appreciation for the world around us with **" The Great Principles of Chemistry."**

Let's promote what's true about our world together.

Warm Regards,

Bill Gray, '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

Peter,
Have you ever heard of the Sinclair Broadcasting Group? Since the late ‘80s, Sinclair, owned by the ultra-conservative Smith family, has been buying up local news stations across the country. **Today, they control an astonishing 190 stations in more than 100 markets. **
As a way to cut costs and push a radical right-wing agenda, Sinclair provides right-wing content to these stations, including “must-run” segments that stations are required to air as a part of their news broadcasts. Through the years, those segments have included everything from propaganda supporting George W. Bush’s invasion of Iraq to stories amplifying Donald Trump’s lies about the “deep state” and the so-called “plot” to undermine his presidency.
**Sinclair’s rise is alarming because according to a 2024 Pew Research study, television is still the most common way voters get local news. **
[**We’ll get into how this dangerous dynamic is playing out in the 2024 election in a moment, but if you’re ready to help COURIER fight back against right-wing propaganda from Sinclair, can you pitch in $20 now?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/88182564/483382679/-593472309?refcode=20240703-EM-SinclairUpdate&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjZlZjk1YWYtNWQzOS1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Dsqe1Cf3zrjgvhN7QgQj_nWtwFbYzspH_hPXctDTPwI=)
So what has Sinclair been up to in 2024?
In June, Sinclair upped its anti-Biden and pro-Trump conspiracies by **partnering with the RNC and the Trump campaign to spread misinformation about Biden’s mental acuity as president. **
They spread edited videos that made it look like Biden couldn’t speak, claimed Biden soiled himself at an event, and said he had to be “led back in” to a G7 summit meeting. When pressed about the blatant propaganda, Sinclair gaslit, claiming it was “outrageous and offensive” to suggest they had any bias.
**Here’s the thing, Peter: Sinclair owns television stations that reach 40% of American households.** And those households aren’t the only ones consuming right-wing misinformation – _Fox News_ and other right-wing media stations repeat the same falsehoods to millions more across the country.
This is where COURIER can help. While Sinclair has been buying up local news outlets, COURIER is providing a freely available alternative in the form of local newsrooms in eleven battleground states around the country.
While Sinclair uses their newsrooms to inject their communities with propaganda, **we use our presence to fight back against misinformation with factual news that actually matters. **
[**But we can’t do it without your help. We don’t rely on paywalls or subscription models to provide our news, which means we need donations from supporters like you to keep fighting back against Sinclair. clean_body: The right-wing media conglomerate uses trusted local news outlets to spread radical propaganda Peter, Have you ever heard of the Sinclair Broadcasting Group? Since the late ‘80s, Sinclair, owned by the ultra-conservative Smith family, has been buying up local news stations across the country. Today, they control an astonishing 190 stations in more than 100 markets. As a way to cut costs and push a radical right-wing agenda, Sinclair provides right-wing content to these stations, including “must-run” segments that stations are required to air as a part of their news broadcasts. Through the years, those segments have included everything from propaganda supporting George W. Bush’s invasion of Iraq to stories amplifying Donald Trump’s lies about the “deep state” and the so-called “plot” to undermine his presidency. Sinclair’s rise is alarming because according to a 2024 Pew Research study, television is still the most common way voters get local news. = So what has Sinclair been up to in 2024? In June, Sinclair upped its anti-Biden and pro-Trump conspiracies by partnering with the RNC and the Trump campaign to spread misinformation about Biden’s mental acuity as president. They spread edited videos that made it look like Biden couldn’t speak, claimed Biden soiled himself at an event, and said he had to be “led back in” to a G7 summit meeting. When pressed about the blatant propaganda, Sinclair gaslit, claiming it was “outrageous and offensive” to suggest they had any bias. Here’s the thing, Peter: Sinclair owns television stations that reach 40% of American households. And those households aren’t the only ones consuming right-wing misinformation – Fox News and other right-wing media stations repeat the same falsehoods to millions more across the country. This is where COURIER can help. While Sinclair has been buying up local news outlets, COURIER is providing a freely available alternative in the form of local newsrooms in eleven battleground states around the country. Peter, you need an ID to get on a plane, drive a car, apply for a loan, and many other things.

Yet, you don’t need one to vote?

Radical Democrats are happy to let illegal immigrants vote, and that should worry all of us.

Folks, we need voter ID laws in all 50 states immediately.

It shouldn’t be complicated. We all want secure and fair elections, and in order to vote in our elections, you should show proof you are a US citizen.

As Election Day grows closer, it’s more and more important that we secure the vote.

# Erin Farris-Olsen for Clerk of the Montana Supreme Court 2024,
**We all know the importance of the Supreme Courts across the country, but do you know about the importance of the Montana Supreme Court Clerk** who helps make sure the Court has the opportunity to review cases without prejudice and do the best job they possibly can?
The Clerk is critical for the Supreme Court to function and remain impartial. [**In Montana I am running for that position for that very reason - and I need your support to win.**](https://erinformontana.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=846aeb55e2fc599e968ca8fae&id=3ecb51f570&e=5e62e9066d)
---
[](https://erinformontana.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=846aeb55e2fc599e968ca8fae&id=2c6efebde6&e=5e62e9066d)
| Montana’s Supreme Court is an institution that has garnered the respect of those who call our State home. For years, the justices have protected our beautiful and unique State Constitution, which includes a strong right to privacy and a clean and healthful environment. Their rulings are what has helped maintain Montana as the Last Best Place.
**Clerks of the court are the first line of support for Montanans seeking justice.**

---
[SUPPORT TODAY!](https://erinformontana.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=846aeb55e2fc599e968ca8fae&id=516c3e0f24&e=5e62e9066d)
|

As an attorney, I have worked for the Montana Supreme Court, and have collaborated with judges, clerks, courts, attorneys, and legal associations across the state improving court efficiencies that also serve people. **We have the chance to ensure that every Montanan gets a fair shake , with a Clerk who can maintain impartiality and objectivity, and protect the integrity of the Judiciary for all Montanans.**
To make that our reality, I just need your help. Campaigning is expensive, and without people like you to support our race, we can’t run the race we need to run to win. [**Your donation, even if only $5, will make a difference in the lives of hundreds of thousands of people.**](https://erinformontana.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=846aeb55e2fc599e968ca8fae&id=848f32314f&e=5e62e9066d)
I know I can count on your support.

---
| Regards,
**Erin**

body:
Today, I want to take a moment to honor our nation’s founding, the Fourth of July, and thank you for all your support during this campaign!

| | | [ ](https://nb.christocongress.com/r?u=vLzcBttMlHPwnhM1pQ23paEVimo0rylpeDdAmHdq2BTK753TLzeZslIp1So4OiurXXYStPcdxa9yIvA10ufNTw&e=826a47930363a3c7550ba96ed32bd779&utm_source=christocongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=1776&n=1)

---
Friend, I want to take a moment to honor our nation’s founding, the Fourth of July, and thank you for all your support during this campaign! I want to extend a special THANK YOU to all our veterans, active-duty military personnel, and their families. They carry on a proud centuries-long tradition of defending Americans’ freedoms and interests, and we all owe them a debt that can never be fully repaid. **If you are out and about over the next two days, come see me and my campaign and, of course, have fun at the Willits Frontier Days in Mendocino County. We'll be there on the 4th. I’ll also be speaking with voters at the Sonoma County GOP HQ on Saturday, the 6th, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. I hope to see you there!** I know I’m not the only candidate asking for your support during this turbulent political cycle, so it means a lot when you extend yourself to supply my campaign with the resources we need to unseat a powerful, well-funded incumbent. **Our nation, state, and region face enormous problems today. But here’s what we don’t face: the mighty British empire. Compared to the task facing the American revolutionaries 248 years ago, our challenges are imminently conquerable.** Yes, our forests are burning, our water sources are under attack, and our communities are grappling with crime, unemployment, and an exodus of working families from a collapsing economy. However, these problems are due to bad leaders and their policies. With our support, good leaders can fix this. Before the fireworks start, **I’m hoping you can make a contribution to my campaign in honor of July 4th with a contribution of[$17.76](https://nb.christocongress.com/r?u=vLzcBttMlHPwnhM1pQ23paEVimo0rylpeDdAmHdq2BTK753TLzeZslIp1So4Oiur1bK2hLCkak8BwKcy3m0Gzw&e=826a47930363a3c7550ba96ed32bd779&utm_source=christocongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=1776&n=2), [$177.6](https://nb.christocongress.com/r?u=vLzcBttMlHPwnhM1pQ23paEVimo0rylpeDdAmHdq2BTK753TLzeZslIp1So4OiurXbUac9ziZbeDe9IjXWfFvw&e=826a47930363a3c7550ba96ed32bd779&utm_source=christocongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=1776&n=3), or even [$1,776](https://nb.christocongress.com/r?u=vLzcBttMlHPwnhM1pQ23paEVimo0rylpeDdAmHdq2BTK753TLzeZslIp1So4OiurUfUHN8Do932PdnNTs_dItQ&e=826a47930363a3c7550ba96ed32bd779&utm_source=christocongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=1776&n=4)**. Any amount helps, and if you can’t give today, that’s okay, too.

Once again, I wish you, your friends, and your family a very Happy Independence Day!

**God Bless the U.S.A.!** **Chris Coulombe
** Republican Candidate for CA-2
